description:
We are a team of curious and motivated students participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Ankara. We are interested in space exploration, technology, coding, artificial intelligence, and game development.

Our goal is to combine creativity, problem-solving, and teamwork to develop an innovative solution for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. We enjoy learning new things, sharing ideas, and turning creative concepts into practical solutions.
summary: THE LAST SIGNAL is an interactive, story-driven space mission game developed by Team INFINITRIO for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Set in the year 2042, players take part in the ASTRA-01 mission to Europa, one of Jupiter’s moons. Throughout the mission, players face difficult decisions, explore scientific discoveries, and experience the challenges of space exploration. Their choices shape the story and influence the mission's outcome. The project combines storytelling, interactive gameplay, and space science to make complex space mission concepts more accessible and engaging. Inspired by real NASA missions and scientific research, THE LAST SIGNAL aims to help students understand the importance of decision-making, problem-solving, and resource management in space exploration.
details:
1. What Does Our Project Do?

THE LAST SIGNAL is a story-driven space mission game set in the year 2042. Players take part in the fictional ASTRA-01 mission to Europa, one of Jupiter's moons. Their goal is to explore Europa and investigate a mysterious signal coming from beneath its icy surface.

Players make important decisions throughout the mission. Each choice can change the story, affect mission resources, and lead to different outcomes. The game includes six chapters, 19 important decision points, a dynamic mission dashboard, and four different endings.

2. How Does It Work?

The game uses an interactive branching story system. Players read mission events, make decisions, and see how their choices affect the next parts of the story.

A mission dashboard displays important information, including energy, mission time, communication, scientific progress, and mission status. These values help players understand the possible effects of their decisions.

The game also includes automatic progress saving, English and Turkish language options, sound effects, and cinematic animations.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

Our main goal is to make space exploration more interesting and easier to understand, especially for students.

THE LAST SIGNAL helps players develop critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills. It also introduces scientific ideas related to Europa and space exploration through an interactive experience.

Instead of only reading about a space mission, players become part of the mission and experience how different decisions can change its outcome.

4. Tools and Technologies

We developed the project as a browser-based web game using:

  • React 18: To build the user interface and interactive game experience.
  • TypeScript: To write structured and reliable code.
  • Vite: To develop and build the application.
  • Tailwind CSS: To design the visual interface.
  • Lucide React: For interface icons.
  • HTML5 Audio and Web Audio API: For music and sound effects.
  • CSS Animations and 3D Transforms: For cinematic visual effects.
  • LocalStorage: To save player progress in the browser.
  • Vercel: To publish the game online.

The game can be played directly through a web browser without downloading a separate application.

5. Creativity and Innovation

Our project combines interactive storytelling with space exploration. We wanted to create an experience where players do not simply follow a fixed story. Instead, they make decisions that influence the mission and its ending.

The dark science-fiction visual style, cinematic transitions, sound design, mission dashboard, and multiple endings make the experience more engaging.

We also created a fictional mission and crew to give players a stronger connection to the story while introducing real scientific concepts.

6. Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific inspiration: We used real NASA missions and research about Europa as inspiration for the game's setting and scientific elements.
  • Player decisions: Choices needed to have meaningful consequences.
  • Mission resources: Energy, time, communication, and scientific progress were included in the mission dashboard.
  • Accessibility: The game supports both English and Turkish.
  • User experience: We aimed to create simple navigation and clear instructions.
  • Performance: The game was developed for web browsers so that players can access it easily.

7. Conclusion

THE LAST SIGNAL brings storytelling, technology, and space science together in one interactive experience. Through the ASTRA-01 mission, we want players to explore the challenges of space exploration and understand how important every decision can be.

Our message is simple: Every choice changes the mission. Every signal tells a story.
